podcast.title: "Nauseating Nancy" by the Press
podcast.body: Due to her loud American attitude and constant presence around the infamous Sex Pistols, Nancy was dubbed "nauseating Nancy" by the press. "Nancy who inserted herself everywhere was dubbed nauseating Nancy by the press because of her loud American attitude."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Birth Complications & Early Trauma
podcast.body: Born Nancy Lauren Spungin on February 27, 1958, in Philadelphia, she nearly died during birth because her umbilical cord was wrapped around her neck, causing cyanosis. She required immediate blood transfusions, suggesting possible oxygen deprivation. "She almost didn't survive her own birth because the umbilical cord was wrapped around her neck, almost choking her, on her way out into the world."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Sid Vicious and Questions About the Murder of Nancy Spungen

podcast.title: Childhood Emotional Disturbances
podcast.body: Nancy displayed emotional problems from an early age, throwing tantrums at three months. By age three, a doctor prescribed barbiturates to control her constant screaming, and she began psychiatric treatment at four. She exhibited violent behavior, including threatening a babysitter with scissors and physically attacking her psychiatrist. "A doctor was worried enough to prescribe baby Nancy barbituates when she was just three in hopes that would stop her from always screaming."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Adult Life in New York
podcast.body: At seventeen, Nancy moved to New York City where she worked as a stripper and occasionally as a prostitute to earn extra money. She became involved in the punk scene, frequenting clubs like CBGB and Max's Kansas City, sometimes carrying drugs for bands. "She moved to New York, where she worked for a while as a stripper, and when she needed extra money, she turned tricks. She was just 17."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Expulsion and Suicide Attempt
podcast.body: She was expelled from school at age eleven and later ran away from her next school, attempting suicide by cutting her wrists with scissors. She escaped from a home for troubled kids where she had been enrolled. "She was expelled from school at eleven. She ran away from her next school and attempted suicide by cutting her wrists with scissors."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Move to London and Groupie Lifestyle
podcast.body: In February 1977, Nancy moved to London, believing it was "where the action was." She fully embraced the groupie lifestyle, with the Sex Pistols as her primary target. "She deterred that that's where the action was. She needed to be there. And Nancy embraced everything she could about the groupie lifestyle."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Murder in the Chelsea Hotel
podcast.body: Nancy Spungin died in Room 100 of the Chelsea Hotel between 8 and 10 AM on October 12, 1978. She was found in the bathroom under the sink, having been stabbed in the lower abdomen with a Jaguar Wilderness K-11 knife, causing fatal external and internal hemorrhaging. The medical examiner concluded it was murder, not suicide. "It was 10.45 on the morning of Thursday, October 12th, 1978. Sid was in shock, initially in a panic. He confessed, I stabbed her, but I never meant to kill her."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Teenage Diagnoses and Ban from Colorado
podcast.body: Diagnosed with schizophrenia at age fifteen, Nancy was also brilliant and enrolled in university in Colorado at sixteen. However, she was thrown out due to "bad and weird behavior," including an arrest for trying to buy pot and accusations of theft. As a result of her issues, she was banished from the state to avoid legal consequences. "Nancy was diagnosed with schizophrenia when she was 15."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Wrist-Cutting Incident in Paris
podcast.body: While Sid was filming parts for "The Great Rock and Roll Swindle" in Paris, Nancy, upset at being left alone in their hotel room, cut her wrists. This was not a serious attempt but rather an act to "make a point." "Nancy was upset at being left alone so she cut her wrists. Nothing serious though. She just wanted to make a point."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Murder at Chelsea Hotel (October 12, 1978)
xref.body: Nancy Spungen, girlfriend of Sid Vicious, was found dead from a single stab wound to her stomach in room 100 of the Chelsea Hotel in New York on October 12, 1978. Nancy had a troubled life, diagnosed with schizophrenia at 15 and supporting herself through prostitution from age 17 before becoming a groupie to bands like The Ramones, New York Dolls, and Aerosmith. She became inseparable from Sid Vicious for 19 months, and they both were heroin and Tuinal addicts. On the night of October 11, 1978, several people visited their room, and Sid allegedly took up to 52 Tuinal tablets, completely incapacitating him. At around 2:30 am on October 12th, Nancy asked Rockets Redglare, their drug connection and Sid's bodyguard, for Dilaudid. Later, around 7:30 am, female moans were heard, and at 10 am, Sid called the front desk. Nancy was found stabbed and bleeding to death, in a weird angle under the bathroom sink. Sid initially confessed but was likely too incapacitated. The theory later emerged that Rockets Redglare, who died in 2007, was the murderer, allegedly stabbing Nancy with Sid's Bowie knife during an argument over stolen cash, a confession he reportedly made while drinking at CBGB. "Nancy Spungin, girlfriend of ex-sex Bristol Sidvicious, at the Chelsea Hotel on October 12, 1978."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: First Meeting with Courtney Love (1989)
xref.body: Kurt Cobain first encountered Courtney Love on January 21, 1989, when Nirvana was performing at the Satiricon Club in Portland, Oregon. Their initial interaction involved Kurt "unceremoniously help[ing] himself to Courtney's picture of beer." Afterwards, Kurt reportedly told friends that Courtney "looked like Nancy Spungin," referring to Sid Vicious's former girlfriend. "Courtney Love first saw Kurt Cobain when Nirvana played a show at the Satiricon Club in Portland, Oregon. The day was January 21st, 1989."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Actor, Drug Dealer, and Key Witness
xref.body: Rockets Red Glare was a drug dealer, bit actor, club bouncer, stand-up comedian, occasional roadie, and sometime police informant. He appeared in over 30 films, including "Desperately Seeking Susan" and "After Hours." He was called by Nancy Spungin for drugs the night she died and is a central figure in alternative theories of her murder, with some alleging he killed her during a robbery. "Let's talk about him for a second. Rockets was an actor who ended up in more than 30 films."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Advocacy for Sid Vicious after Nancy's Death
xref.body: After Nancy Spungin's murder and Sid Vicious's arrest, Malcolm McLaren and Sid's mother immediately sought a high-profile lawyer for his defense. McLaren strongly believed Sid was innocent, theorizing that an unknown guest had robbed the couple and then stabbed Nancy, noting that $20,000 in royalty money was missing from their room. "McLaren thought that Sid was innocent. He had a theory. He thought that the couple was robbed by an unknown guest who then stabbed Nancy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Sid Vicious and Questions About the Murder of Nancy Spungen

xref.title: Alternative Murder Suspect
xref.body: The most popular alternative theory states that Rockets Red Glare murdered Nancy Spungin while Sid Vicious was incapacitated by drugs, in the process of robbing the couple of $1400 (and an alleged $20,000 in royalties). Author Phil Strongman's book "Pretty Vacant" advances this theory, citing Red Glare's sudden acquisition of money and new clothes shortly after Nancy's death, despite previously being broke. "The most popular alternative theory is that Nancy was killed by Rockets Red Glare."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Aspiring Singer & Nancy Spungin's Friend
xref.body: Neon Leon Webster was an aspiring singer and the boyfriend of Kathy O'Rourke, a friend of Nancy Spungin. He and Kathy visited Sid and Nancy in Room 119 of the Chelsea Hotel on the night Nancy died, and he later provided a disputed account of his whereabouts that night. "At 945, the couple went down the hall to Room 119, where they visited with Kathy or Rourke, a friend of Nancy's, and Neon Leon Webster, an aspiring singer and her boyfriend."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Death at 21 Years Old – Before Murder Trial
xref.body: Sid Vicious died at the age of 21 on February 2, 1979, from a heroin overdose. His death occurred before he could stand trial for the murder of Nancy Spungen, leading the New York police to close the case. "Sid was dead before he got to go to trial for the murder of Nancy Spungin."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Nancy Spungin's Attempted Backing Vocals
xref.body: Nancy Spungin insisted on singing backup vocals at the Vicious White Kids' gig, but the sound engineer deliberately turned off her microphone. "He insisted on singing backup vocals, but the sound guy made sure her mic was turned off."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Relationship with Nancy Spungen
xref.body: Kurt Cobain remarked that Courtney Love reminded him of Nancy Spungen, identifying her as Sid Vicious's "old girlfriend." This comparison highlighted a perceived shared aesthetic or personality trait between Courtney Love and Spungen. "I thought she looked like Nancy Spungin. She was, seduicious as old girlfriend before somebody, maybe said, killed her."
